tag: Episode 1 · I Became a Flower Pig
title: I Became a Flower Pig

beats.t: Her fall softened, and light wrapped around her. Her arms shortened; her fingers grew blunt. When she opened her eyes, Yeoni was in the middle of a huge lotus-leaf boat floating on a river.
I TURNED INTO A PIIIIIG!
Her scream stretched across the night-dark river, then cut off. This body barely had the lung capacity to scream.
The leaf was wider than her bed at home. Dew glimmered along its edges like little lamps. No oars, sail, or engine—just an enormous lotus leaf, floating steadily.
Yeoni stared down at herself. Short forelegs. Round belly. Curly tail. A small flower on her head. However she looked at it, this pink body wasn't human.
No. …How am I supposed to do my assignments with these?
An odd sound slipped into the end of her sentence.
This makes absolutely no sense, oink.
Yeoni froze.
...What was that?
Hello. I am a human being.
That came out fine. Yeoni felt a little relieved.
Okay. Talking works. That's something.
Then she looked at her forelegs again.
…My fingers are gone.
This is clearly a downgrade. From a human with ten fingers to a pig with two forelegs.
A moment ago she'd been in her room. Wet socks, a strange app, a tarot door. Now she was a pig with a flower. A flower pig, to be precise.
She plopped onto the leaf. Her soft body squished, then sprang back. The sensation was so vivid it made things worse.
Okay. Got it. …This is a dream.
Even with the world as strange as it was these days, turning into a flower pig after one wrong tap on an app was going too far.
Yeoni tapped the leaf with a forehoof. She could feel it.
In a dream, you're supposed to pinch yourself awake. …My hoof won't reach my face.
...Nice graphics, though.
Yeoni reached a very serious conclusion. She'd played a limited-time event until three last night. This was gaming fallout.
Status window.
Nothing appeared.
Menu. ...Inventory.
Only the wind passed. Yeoni narrowed their eyes.
...Terrible UI. One star.
Then a low voice came from the end of the leaf.
Still think it's a dream? Understandable.
Yeoni froze, then slowly turned her head. Something was sitting at the leaf's edge.
At first she thought it was a white cat: small, round, and fluffy. But it wore a navy wizard's hat with a golden crescent moon. Later, Yeoni would call this cat Yeongnyangi.
...What are you?
I'm in charge of this river.
A cat?
No.
Then what? You look exactly like a cat in a hat.
If you must know, I'm no ordinary cat.
Then why are you so tiny? You'd fit in my palm.
Yeongnyangi's whiskers twitched.
…Rather harsh for a first meeting.
I was just dragged into another world and turned into a pig. Today, I think I've earned the right to be rude.
Yeongnyangi fell silent for a moment.
…Fair enough.
Are you an NPC?
No.
That's what all NPCs say.
…Now that you mention it, that sounded like an NPC too.
I am the guardian of the River of Four Pillars.
...An NPC with lore, then.
Yeoni pressed a hoof to the flower on her head. Five petals trembled. She could feel them far too clearly.
Wow. The detail is insane.
Does it hurt?
No. It just feels weird.
Then it is real.
That is a ridiculously sloppy test.
Rather than answer, Yeongnyangi looked beyond the boat. Yeoni followed his gaze. Only then did she really see where she was.

A river. Its water was as deep blue as the night sky, starlight breaking on every ripple. Unfamiliar characters swam through it like fish: 甲子, 乙丑, 丙寅, 丁卯. The sort of characters she'd give up on the moment they appeared on an exam.
Mist hung in the distance, with shapes like pillars dimly standing beyond it. A large moon filled the sky. Its light wasn't cold. It was impossibly beautiful, and that frightened her.
You could wake from a dream. Quit a game. But this felt like a dream she didn't know how to wake from or switch off.
...Where is this?
The River of Four Pillars.
Four Pillars? Like saju?
The place where the codes of human destiny flow.
Right. I understood none of that.
Normal. Most humans are like that when they first arrive.
I'm not human anymore.
A flower pig, to be precise.
I hate that word more every time I hear it.
Better than an ordinary pig, isn't it?
...Is that meant to comfort me?
An objective analysis.
Yeoni drew a deep breath. A little snort escaped. Oink. Hearing that come from her own mouth suddenly made her furious.
Why a pig, of all things! ...And where am I? I want to go home.
That will not be easy.
I wasn't expecting an easy answer.
Yeongnyangi walked slowly across the leaf. Each step made it glow. Star-shaped marks tipped his pink pads. Perhaps he was more than a cat who said strange things.
Hey, Hat. Are you responsible for this place?
Something like that.
Then I'm filing a complaint. Turning me into a pig for tapping an app is excessive, isn't it?
You are rather cute.
Another complaint. …What I tapped was an app. Code Something.
Yeongnyangi's expression stiffened a little.
That was a door.
Looked like an app.
It took a shape humans would tap. You might not open a door, but you'd tap an app.
Yeoni fell silent. She couldn't think of a single argument.
The water beneath the boat suddenly heaved. Splash. Yeoni ducked instinctively.
What was that?
Yeongnyangi's eyes changed. Their bored-cat violet spread into gold, and the crescent on his hat glowed faintly.
Residue of misfortune. Leaking from your reality.
My... reality?
He pointed toward the spreading black ink. The dark water swallowed passing characters one by one. Their light blackened and twisted.
Your luck's been going wrong lately.
Silent alarms. A card rejected three times. A rice triangle with the wrong filling. A broken assignment file. An app that wouldn't delete. Yeoni had no words.
She'd laughed them all off, but they kept catching somewhere inside her. Why this much bad luck? Why did everything keep missing her by a fraction?
Does that... have something to do with this place?
Your destiny code is damaged. The characters of your Four Pillars have scattered.
Someone tampered with my Four Pillars? Why bother? What's even in there?
To learn that, you must recover your characters first.

Before he finished, a black hand burst from the river. Each finger held something: a rice-triangle wrapper showing spicy pork, a worn transit card, a broken assignment-file icon. The hand of black water reached for the leaf's rim.
Yeoni froze. Every joke she'd been forcing herself to hold onto vanished. This wasn't dream scenery. Something was coming to take her.
Is that... coming for me?
Yes.
Why?
Because you are its target.
How can you say that so calmly!
The black hand reached over the boat. Yeoni tried to retreat, but her body still felt borrowed. Her short legs scrambled uselessly on the leaf.
Why are this body's controls so awful!
You'll get used to the controls.
Just as the hand reached her, Yeongnyangi vanished. A golden line sliced the air. Shrrk. The hand split in two, scattering drops of ink.
Yeongnyangi landed at the leaf's edge. His body could fit in a palm. There had been nothing small about that movement.
Don't call me just a cat again. I'm no ordinary cat.
Yeoni considered that for a moment.
...Combat cat?
The cat's eyes narrowed.
Guardians don't reveal their names. Customer-service rules. Call me whatever you like.
Then Yeongnyangi. A mystical little kitty. I'll stake one star on my naming skills.
The hands didn't disappear. Their severed pieces melted into the water, then gathered into thicker, longer shapes.
Yeongnyangi tapped the leaf. Transparent droplets rose around its edge like little shields. The black hands scraped them with a piercing screech.
...Worst sound ever.
They will not hold for long.
Then what do we do?
The flower on your head is alive.
Yeoni touched the flower. It glowed very faintly, small but unmistakably warm.
What is it?
A trace of your Day Master. The central character that represents you.
Yeoni immediately gave up trying to understand.
Okay. For now, my flower's a battery.
It is not.
I'm putting it in terms I understand.
A wrong understanding is dangerous.
You explain things like a compulsory-course professor.
The black hands approached again. Yeongnyangi looked across the river. Four lights rose in the mist.
One shone a sharp blue. One flickered like warm fire. One flashed gold. The last glowed softly, like an old bookshelf.
Your characters scattered to four places. Each of those lights belongs to you.
Yeoni watched them. Too vivid for a dream, too chilling for a game. Yet the lights seemed to be calling her.
So I have to collect them all to get home.
Yes.
Wait. I never agreed to any terms.
There is no consent procedure.
Can I get a refund halfway through?
No.
A help forum?
No.
Customer support?
…I am here, in my own way.
...That makes me incredibly nervous.
Complaints are not accepted.
Worst customer service ever.
Neither are star ratings.
Then a black hand broke through the shield. It held the transit card with worn corners.
OINK—AAH!
Yeoni immediately covered their mouth.
…That was because I was startled.
I know.
Behind me. Stay hidden.
Yeoni started to duck behind him, then stopped. The transit card glittered between black fingers. Beep, please try again. The sound rang in her ears.
…No. That's my complaint.
She stepped beside Yeongnyangi. Her short legs shook. Her voice didn't.
Transit card, one star! Four attempts to work. Would not buy again!
[ Complaint resolved · Transit card · One star ]
The flower flared. Light seeped between the black fingers, melting the transit card like candle wax. The empty hand clutched at the air, then unraveled into ink.
…You did that.
Me? With a star rating?
Before he answered, a chill touched the top of her head. Yeoni felt for her flower. One of its five petals had faded paper-white.
Wait. Was it always like this?
The cost of drawing on your light. That petal won't return easily.
…You said no refunds.
None. Use it sparingly.
Yeongnyangi leapt through the opening. Golden markings flashed on his claws: Four Pillars Starlight. He swept a paw, and a blade of starlight cut across the river, severing all the remaining hands.
The leaf boat surged forward. The river parted to open a path. As soon as he landed, Yeongnyangi spoke under his breath.
…I won't lose you.
Before Yeoni could ask, Yeongnyangi pointed beyond the mist. The bow slowly turned that way.
Let's start with that sharp light.
Why there?
It looks the scariest. Scary things get less scary if you do them first.
…Where I was headed anyway. The Island of Companions.
Companions? Bad name already.
She watched the first light in the mist. It was less beautiful than sharp, like glass. Close enough, and it might cut her.
…Explain when we get there. Hearing it now might scare me.
When we arrive. Briefly.
I don't trust your definition of briefly.
I'll try.
The leaf boat sped up. Behind them, black hands tore through the river again. Ahead, the mist thickened, and an island's shadow slowly emerged.
Countless little mirror shards floated around the island. In one, Yeoni in a hoodie was waving at her. With a human hand.
